app.title: OpenCode Monitor
update.title: A newer version of this page is available
update.body: The monitor was updated while this page was open. Reload to see the new version.
conn.stale: Can't read OpenCode's data right now — showing the last good reading
reason.question: The agent asked a question
reason.tool_long: One tool call has been running for more than {limit}
reason.length: The reply hit the output token limit
reason.not_running: OpenCode closed while this was in progress
hint.many_compactions: Compacted {n} times, so early details are probably lost.
hint.old_session: This session has been open for {t}.
hint.looping: The same {tool} call ran {n} times recently: {text}
env.mcp.tip.failed: OpenCode logged this server failing, and none of its tools has worked since.
env.mcp.tip.ok: One of this server's tools completed recently.
env.mcp.tip.unknown: No failure logged and no tool of this server used in the sessions shown, so there is nothing to judge by.
env.title: What the agent depends on
work.title: Work
work.protected: This session is working directly on {branch}. Changes made through shell commands are not counted in the files above.
work.recentFiles: Latest files touched by the agent
work.unknownBranch: The current branch could not be read, so there is no check for a protected branch.
work.unreadable: There is a repository here, but its branch was not read: it is a worktree or submodule, .git or HEAD is not a plain directory and file, or the read failed. Nothing about it is known, so nothing is assumed to be fine.
work.runningTitle: Started in the background by this session, and still running
work.runningNote: Matched by start time and command words, so check the command before stopping anything. The monitor never stops processes itself.
review.title: To review
review.note: Found by matching text. It can miss a command written in an unusual way, so an empty list is not proof that nothing risky ran.
review.hiddenExamples: {n} more distinct commands in this group are not shown.
review.more: {n} more flagged calls of other kinds are not shown.
review.ignored: {n} matches left out by review.ignoreRules in your config.
rule.hidden_command: Built at run time, could not be checked
rule.git_internals: Changes git's own records or config
approval.asked: you were asked, then it ran
approval.rule: allowed by a rule, no prompt
theme.label: Theme
history.emptyBody: Each change of state is recorded here while the monitor is running.
history.truncated: Older entries are kept only in data/history.jsonl.
links.label: More about "{title}"
stats.source: From OpenCode's own records, including days when the monitor was not running.
stats.sourceSession: Only this session and its subagents, from OpenCode's own records.
stats.failed: The figures could not be read from OpenCode's database. They are retried every minute.
stats.mcpOffList: Switched off, with nothing to report:
stats.question: Question
stats.abandoned: never answered; OpenCode moved on or closed
stats.slowestNote: Time spent waiting for your permission is not counted.
stats.noSlow: No tool calls in this period.
stats.graftShare: graft was used for {pct}% of code lookups ({graft} graft calls, {other} read, grep, or glob).
stats.rereadsNote: Read 3 or more times in the same session.
stats.noRereads: No file was read 3 or more times in one session.
stats.abandonedNote: {prompts} prompts and {calls} tool calls were left unfinished when a session moved on or OpenCode closed. They are not counted as waiting or as slow.
stats.contextNote: Size of each of its {n} requests, in order. Dashed lines are compactions.
stats.contextNoCompaction: This session was not compacted in the period.
compare.label: Compare before and after a day
compare.title: Before and after
compare.heading: Before and after {day}
compare.note: For a setting you changed that day. Rates and typical values only, because the two sides are rarely the same length.
compare.thin: One side has fewer than 3 sessions. Treat the differences as a first hint, not a result.
compare.none: Nothing to compare: that day is outside the period, or is its first day.
compare.metric.firstTokenMs: Typical wait for the first token
stats.speedNote: Writing is timed from the first token to the last thing the model wrote; tools running and prompts waiting for you are not in it. Reading is the wait for the first token, over the new part of the prompt.
stats.speedFirst: Typical wait for the first token
stats.usageNote: As reported by the model server, over {n} requests.
stats.usageNewNote: had to be processed from scratch
stats.usageStartLine: A session starts at about {median} tokens (typical of {n} sessions).
stats.usageStartNote: The starting size is the first request of a session: instructions, skills, and the tool list of every MCP server that is switched on, before any work is done. It is part of every later request too, so it also sets how much of the context window is left for the work.
stats.mcpNote: "failed" is a tool reporting an error; "no answer" is the server itself not responding. Open a row to see its tools.
stats.mcpUnused: Switched on but never called in this period: {names}. Each one still adds its tool list to every prompt; consider switching it off globally and on per project.
stats.mcpUnusedSession: Switched on but never called in this session: {names}.
stats.mcpNoLogForSession: Dropped connections and failed starts are not shown for a single session: OpenCode's log does not say which session they happened in.
stats.mcpLogFrom: OpenCode's log only goes back to {t}; dropped connections and failed starts before that are not counted.
empty.title: No recent sessions
empty.body: Sessions active in the last {h} hours appear here.
notify.env.body: The agent may keep going without it. Check the monitor.
notify.test.title: opencode-monitor test
notify.test.body: If you can read this, notifications reach you.
